# Adaptive Workout Coach

Adaptive Workout Coach is a lightweight guided workout app: pure HTML, CSS,
and JavaScript, no build step, no server, no accounts. It runs as a static
site (GitHub Pages serves the docs/ folder). Open the URL and follow the
30-minute session, three times per week, even with no routine, no plan, and
no experience. Every exercise tells the user exactly what to do, in what
order, with big legible dose labels (sets x reps), muscle-group tags, and
demo video links where verified demos exist. No expertise required.

## The program

A 3-phase program, about 3 weeks per phase, 3 sessions per week. It is a
workout companion for someone returning after a long time off their feet,
not a personal prescription. Start only after a physical therapist or
physician has cleared resistance training.

Phase 1 "Reactivate" (12 exercises): isometric strength, glute activation,
balance, no deep loaded knee bending. Phase 2 "Reload" (11 exercises): light
loaded patterns, bilateral before unilateral. Phase 3 "Return" (14
exercises): the full routine, including a bodyweight Bulgarian split squat
that starts at 3 x 6 each side, plus lateral step-downs and reverse lunges.

Moving up a phase uses Advance only, after 9 logged sessions and every
checklist item for that phase. Moving back is always allowed. Weeks are
minimums. Week 1, 2, and 3 doses sit inside each phase. A flagged session
(pain above 2/10 during, next-morning pain, or next-morning swelling) does
not move the week and, twice in a row, turns Advance off. The app never
ticks the checklist from those scores and never rewrites the dose text.
No running or plyometrics until separately cleared.

## What the app does

- Runs a guided 30-minute workout with a single stored timer deadline, so
  closing and reopening the browser resumes with the correct time left.
- Full session lifecycle: start (after a clearance confirmation), pause,
  resume, clear (with confirmation), finish (pain check-in, then log),
  timer expiry, and "Something's wrong" (stop without logging).
- Per-exercise checklists, accordion sections, progress bar, sticky status
  bar, big dose labels.
- Tue-Sat gym calendar (Sundays are for church, Mondays are rest) with a
  configurable third gym day; completed days log toward the 3-per-week goal.
- A red-flag panel stays on the page: giving way, locking or catching, a hot
  or markedly swollen knee, night pain, calf pain or swelling.
- Demo videos come from a topic-organized video library
  (docs/video-library.js). To swap an exercise's videos, edit only that file
  or the exercise's demo_ids. Demo URLs are only added when verified, never
  invented.
- All progress is stored in the browser's localStorage under awc-demo-v1.
  No accounts, no analytics, no tracking, no personal data. Unreadable saves
  are backed up in the browser, the user is told, and only the latest few
  backups are kept.

## Project layout

- docs/index.html: app shell (status bar, timer, routine, calendar,
  phase picker, checklist, clearance, red flags). A Content-Security-Policy
  meta tag limits the page to its own files.
- docs/styles.css: styles, native CSS, light/dark aware.
- docs/app.js: all app logic: phases, timer, calendar, checklist,
  progression, symptoms. Progress persists in localStorage.
- docs/video-library.js: topic-organized demo video library. This is the
  file to edit when swapping videos.
- test/: node:test suites. Run with npm test. Not served from docs/.
- .github/workflows/test.yml: npm ci and npm test on pull requests.
- README.md: full documentation.
- FEATURES.md: feature list with status and location.
- llms.txt: this file.

## How to run it

Live: https://jhanisusM.github.io/adaptive-workout-coach/ (GitHub Pages,
deploys from docs/ on every push to main).

Locally: serve the docs/ folder with any static file server, e.g.
`cd docs && python3 -m http.server 8000`, then open http://localhost:8000.

Tests: `npm test` from the repository root.

## Safety

This is a workout companion, not medical advice. The app tells users to train
within a comfortable range, that sharp pain is a stop sign, and to follow
their clinician's guidance when training around an injury or condition.
The source is public on GitHub. All rights reserved.
